questions.prompt: You rename a Bicep symbolic identifier from store to archive, updating all code references but retaining the resource type, Azure name, scope, and properties. What does this change itself do?

options.text: Refactors the code without changing the Azure resource identity.
options.explanation: The deployed identity uses type, name, and scope, not the local symbol.

options.text: Renames the deployed account to archive.
options.explanation: The Azure name property was retained.

options.text: Deletes the resource formerly represented by store.
options.explanation: Changing only the symbol does not request deletion.

options.text: Moves the resource into a deployment named archive.
options.explanation: A symbolic identifier does not select deployment scope or history name.

questions.prompt: What does a successful az bicep build establish before an Azure deployment?

options.text: The file can compile to an ARM template.
options.explanation: Build performs compilation and reports Bicep diagnostics.

options.text: The deployment identity has all required Azure permissions.
options.explanation: Local compilation does not establish RBAC access.

options.text: The target region has capacity for every VM.
options.explanation: Allocation happens during deployment, not compilation.

options.text: All Azure Policy assignments permit the resources.
options.explanation: Policy evaluation depends on the Azure scope and resource request.

questions.prompt: A Bicep file is deployed to rg-app. Virtual network vnet-shared already exists in rg-network in the same subscription. The file declares that network using existing, name: 'vnet-shared', and scope: resourceGroup('rg-network'), then reads its properties. No resource or role assignments are declared for that network. Which TWO statements describe this configuration? Evaluate each statement individually.

options.text: The declaration references vnet-shared without redeploying it.
options.explanation: existing references the resource already at the specified name and scope; it does not create or update it.

options.text: The lookup targets rg-network rather than rg-app.
options.explanation: The explicit resourceGroup scope selects the group containing the network instead of the deployment target group.

options.text: The lookup creates vnet-shared in rg-app if it is missing in rg-network.
options.explanation: The existing declaration has neither provisioning behavior nor a fallback to the deployment resource group.

options.text: The declaration grants the deployment identity permission to read vnet-shared.
options.explanation: Referencing a resource does not create a role assignment. The identity needs appropriate existing access.
